claim: Strategy selection can be written as a contextual bandit: per strategy, learn from cheap problem features a model of expected reward and a model of run time, then pick the strategy with the best reward minus time cost (VOC). In sorting this beat the best prior selectors (99.78% vs 98.5% best-algorithm choice; 88.1% of maximal speed vs at most 30% for nine psychological models). One lab, simulation on generated lists.
agent_test: Build a per-class table of pass rate and token cost from our logs; choose mode by argmax(pass - lambda*tokens); compare with always-same-mode at equal total tokens.

claim: People pick the strategy that fits the problem, not just the one with the best average payoff. Mixed environments where one fixed strategy gives chance: 76.2% agreement with the right strategy (N=100, 100 trials; 73% already on trial 1) and 64.6% vs 50% (N=120, 30 trials, no learning slope). Both from one lab; trial-1 success points to prior knowledge, and one general strategy might do well on both problem kinds.
agent_test: Mixed-class benchmark where the best mode differs by class and one fixed mode scores near chance. Context-free (per-mode average) selector vs feature-based selector at equal tokens.

claim: On quantitative fit the simple context-free reinforcement model (SSL) is as good as or better than feature-based metareasoning in homogeneous environments: MSE 0.0050 vs 0.0048 (2015); BIC 60.70 (SSL) vs 68.94 (RM), MSE 0.0018 vs 0.0043 (2017, same Rieskamp and Otto data). Features only pay when the environment is mixed. The two papers disagree on how close the tie is.
agent_test: In a single-class stream, compare a feature-free running average per mode with the feature table: expect a tie; add features only where classes mix.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Pure cost-benefit and pure reinforcement accounts each fail a test: people start with the costly full-information strategy (Newell et al. data, 24 people, SSL mean p=.71), and they switch slowly and asymmetrically after an environment change (27% moved to compensatory, 65% to TTB; SSL predicted about 100 extra trials, real switching faster). Metareasoning start-up behaviour was fitted, not predicted. Reanalyses by the SSL author.
agent_test: Log how fast a class table adapts after a distribution shift (a new problem family); test change detection that resets stale class records.

claim: Thinking amount follows opportunity cost in humans. High reward rate leads to less information gathering (engagement 37% to 19%, N=100), and when low-stakes games become the only earner people engage more (N=144, d=0.26). Time cost shrinks and error cost grows anchoring adjustment (50.7% to 31.0%; 31.6% to 50.1%; N=30 after exclusions), but effects are small (error cost only 3 points for provided anchors, N=60 recruited) and the provided-anchor result contradicts Epley and Gilovich 2006 while agreeing with Simmons 2010.
agent_test: Vary the token price lambda in the gate and check that the share of long modes falls as lambda rises; fit lambda per class.

claim: Planning strategy tracks the environment's payoff structure (variance rising vs falling with depth: first click on an end state 95.0% vs 0.3%; optimal model best in 2 of 3 conditions, N=298), with systematic departures. All versions from one lab; best-first was near-optimal in the constant condition so models are hard to separate.
agent_test: Per-class check of whether the best mode changes with a cheap structure cue; the class record must key on that cue.

claim: Feedback on the quality of the planning process (delay penalty plus a hint of the best step) lifts human planning near optimal while feedback on actions does not: 94.4 vs 77.0 vs 73.5 (d=0.59, N=151); delayed transfer 81.2 vs 49.0 vs 57.6 (N=297); both parts needed (87.5 vs 75.8, d=0.32; delay only d=0.05, hint only d=-0.09). Far transfer weak (46.3% vs 39.4%, d=0.17). Effects shrink as designs tighten; all one lab, no outside replication seen.
agent_test: Log per-step process feedback (which mode wasted tokens, which would have passed) into the class record, vs logging only final correctness; compare class-table quality at equal logged runs.

claim: Without a tutor people rarely discover a new useful planning strategy (0.79% to 28.57% over 120 trials, N=349) and strategy learning looks like gradient-style learning (REINFORCE family 47.41% of learners; non-learners best for 34% of all), but the mechanism is unsettled and extra-mechanism variants fit 70% better (same dataset). The 2017 model assumes a fixed strategy set.
agent_test: Do not rely on the agent inventing modes online; keep a fixed small mode set and test whether adding a fifth mode helps.

claim: Rational-metareasoning-style training of an LLM (reward = log-probability gain minus lambda*length) cuts output tokens at equal or better accuracy and makes length depend on difficulty. Re-checked against the paper: 35-42% fewer tokens than few-shot, 23-32% fewer than STaR; hard vs easy length drop 50.3% (RaM) vs 34.4% (STaR) vs 19.0% (few-shot CoT) vs 0.5% (instruct CoT). Out of domain 28-36% fewer tokens, but one model lost 3.8 accuracy points (40.2 to 36.4, intervals overlap). Needs fine-tuning, so not usable in the scaffold as is; easy defined by few-shot success.
agent_test: Prompt-only analogue: cap tokens per class by the class's easy/hard record and compare accuracy at equal tokens with a uniform cap.

claim: Adaptive allocation of reasoning effort or model choice, learned from logged outcomes, cuts cost at about equal quality across independent labs and settings: ARES (TAU-Bench Retail 54.8 = High 54.8; 52.7% fewer reasoning tokens; BrowseComp-Plus 41.3 vs 42.7 with 41.8% fewer), RouteLLM (MT-Bench 95% of GPT-4, over 2x cheaper), FrugalGPT (up to 98% cost cut or +4% at same cost), R2-Router (4-5x cheaper), Thinkless (50-90% fewer long chains). Most need training and an answer scorer; some gains over fixed-high are small.
agent_test: Class-table router (code only) vs fixed high effort vs fixed low at equal total tokens; report pass rate per 1000 tokens.
audit_note: Minor: ARES token reductions are 'up to' 52.7% on TAU-Bench (35.2% in total reasoning tokens on Retail); R2-Router 4-5x taken from the abstract.

claim: More thinking is not always better, so a fixed high-effort policy is not the optimum: TAU-Bench Airline High 38.0 vs Medium 42.0; reasoning mode hurts on safety and knowledge items in judging; named strategies do not beat no-strategy (47.2% vs 45.1-49.0%). Small test sets (about 50 tasks in Airline). Added in gap search: Snell et al. find beam search against a process reward model gets worse with budget on easy MATH bins; Chen et al. find the first solution round is correct in over 92% of cases and uses under 60% of tokens.
agent_test: Check on our own classes whether the short mode beats the long mode on easy and knowledge classes; the gate should choose short there.

claim: Asking the model to choose its own mode or strategy fails: Qwen3 judges choose reasoning 99.5-99.9% of the time (accuracy near all-reasoning, cost 6.25 to 19.07 times all-instruct); direct LLM arm selection is weaker than a LinUCB bandit (Game of 24: 82 vs 89); GPT-5 as router 40.0 vs ARES 54.8 on Retail; models cannot pick the per-item best strategy though an oracle would gain a lot (TruthQuest 47.2% to 82.9%).
agent_test: Compare an LLM-chosen mode with the code-chosen class-table mode at equal tokens; count the share of the long mode chosen.

claim: The oracle gap between strategies is mostly not recovered by post-hoc selection: majority vote 54.9, vote+prob 57.3, verifier 46.9 (Phi-4 TruthQuest) vs oracle 82.9; no selection rule wins everywhere (R1-Distill: verifier 74.1, vote 68.4). Part of the vote gain is plain noise averaging (G4), so the oracle is an inflated bound. Values re-checked in the paper. Gap search: the oracle is any-of-five prompts with no same-sample-count control; Brown et al. show any-of-k coverage rises log-linearly with k alone (MATH Llama-3-8B 82.9% at 100 samples to 98.44% at 10,000, while vote or reward model moved 40.50% to 41.41%). The gap shrinks on hard items (Zhang difficulty split), so part is predictable by size.
agent_test: Report best-single, vote and oracle per class; only the part of the gap above vote at equal samples counts as selection value. Control: any-of-k of one mode vs any-of-k across k modes, repeated runs per item.

claim: A cue-based gate can invert: the sign of the link between token entropy and the benefit of extra compute flips across environments and backbones (Spearman -0.346 to +0.428). Learning the direction per (environment, backbone) from counterfactual runs gives the best success in 16 of 18 cells, but in some cells always-trigger is still better (37.0 base, 59.8 always, 49.8 DIAL).
agent_test: Never hard-code the cue direction; estimate it per class from our own paired runs with and without extra compute.

claim: LLMs shift strategy with problem size: enumeration to elimination as the hypothesis space grows (beta log size +1.0212, beta trials -0.1466, both p<.001; pseudo R2 0.160; judge kappa 0.76; values re-checked), with little shift on XOR. This is size tracking with weak fit, not shown to be cost-optimal; no human data.
agent_test: Use problem size as one cheap class feature in the table; test whether it predicts which mode wins.

claim: Bandit or UCB selection of thinking strategies per question improves over CoT and best-of-N (Game of 24: 89 for GPT-4o-mini vs ToT 65; MetaScale Arena-Hard GPT-4o 93.14 vs CoT 84.72), but rewards in both are LLM scored or LLM judged, which G5 and G8 distrust; benchmarks are mostly maths puzzles and style-sensitive judging.
agent_test: Run a Thompson-sampling selector over modes using code-checked rewards only; compare with an LLM-judged-reward variant.

claim: Small single-author router results (3-mode router +1.0 on GSM8K with n=50 per set; monitor-generate-verify 75.42% vs 68.44% on GSM8K, 659 items, single run) are within noise or preliminary and are not usable as support.
agent_test: Do not cite. Re-test only on a larger set.

claim: The full formal metareasoning policy (BMPS) is near-optimal on synthetic metalevel problems (99.1% of optimal planning-tree return; at most 5.19% below optimal on a Bernoulli bandit) but needs an exact model of the agent's own belief updates, so it is not directly usable for an LLM; the learned linear mix reduces to myopic VOI plus cost when cost is high.
agent_test: Not testable directly; the practical analogue is a linear score from two cheap features and a cost term.

claim: A class table that must keep learning after the problem mix changes needs forgetting. Stationary bandits stop exploring; sliding-window or discounted UCB reach regret of order sqrt(T) log T with a fixed number of changes, and a Thompson sampler with a Beta posterior that decays toward the prior keeps reasonable regret in a drifting Bernoulli simulation (gamma=0.01, 10,000 runs). Best window shrinks as change gets more frequent. Theory and simulation only; no LLM-routing test.
agent_test: Replay logs with a mid-log shift in the class mix; compare no decay, window and decay gamma in {0.01, 0.05}; report tokens to recover the global-mode pass rate.

claim: Allocating compute by a difficulty class beats uniform allocation: five bins by the base model's own pass@1, best strategy per bin, beat best-of-N at about 4x less compute on MATH; on easy bins beam search against the process reward model gets worse with budget. But the difficulty estimate used 2048 samples per question and its cost was not counted. Shows the per-class shape; difficulty must be learned from running logs to be free.
agent_test: Use the running per-class pass rate as the difficulty feature; count all estimation tokens in the comparison with fixed modes.

claim: The token price lambda can be set by the budget instead of by hand: RACER updates a Lagrange multiplier by primal-dual steps, it rises under tight budgets and goes to zero when the budget stops binding (budgets C=2 to 10, 20 repeats; beats three routers by 0.64-1.10 points at C=4). One author group, judge tasks, neural router; not tested against the best fixed budget.
agent_test: Run the table with lambda as a dual variable that targets a token budget; compare with each fixed lambda and with the best fixed mode at the same total tokens.

claim: Gap not closed: no independent replication of the 2017 strategy-selection experiments was found, because web search was unavailable in this run. Absence of evidence only.
agent_test: Retry the search when quota returns; do not cite K02 or K03 as replicated.
